chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from his father (peace be upon them). He said:

Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) visited Harun al-Rashid, and anger had overwhelmed him against a man. So he said to him: You only get angry for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so do not get angrier on His behalf than He gets for Himself.

key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: the Mighty and Majestic (epithet of God)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim say to Harun al-Rashid about controlling anger?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) counsels Harun al-Rashid on the proper limits of righteous anger. When the caliph was furious at someone, the Imam reminded him that if his anger is truly for God's sake, he should not exceed the measure of God's own displeasure, since God Himself is more merciful than wrathful. This teaching establishes a profound principle of emotional moderation: even justified anger must be proportionate and restrained.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d al-Abidi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi `Abdullah al-Barqi from `Abd al-Athim b. `Abdullah al-Hasani from Muhammad b. `Ali b. Musa b. Ja`far b. Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. `Ali b. Abi Talib from his father (as). He said:
Musa b. Ja`far (as) visited Harun al-Rashid, and he eased his anger against a man. So, he said to him: Only get angry for the sake of Allah. Do not get angrier on His behalf than He gets for Himself.
